report.title: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 4.8 with adaptive thinking and 84% browser-agent score
report.summary: Claude Opus 4.8 is now generally available via API and on Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plans, priced at $5/M input and $25/M output tokens. It introduces adaptive thinking (auto-scales reasoning depth by task), tops CursorBench across every effort level, scores 84% on Online-Mind2Web, and is the only model to complete every case on Anthropic's Super-Agent benchmark — beating GPT-5.5 at cost parity.

report.title: Anthropic commits Claude will remain ad-free permanently
report.summary: Anthropic published a policy post explaining it will not introduce advertising to Claude, arguing ad incentives are structurally incompatible with a trustworthy assistant. Meaningful for enterprise buyers and consumer trust positioning, but no API or product change ships with the announcement.

report.title: Claude Cowork goes GA on macOS and Windows with new Enterprise Analytics API
report.summary: Anthropic made Claude Cowork generally available on the desktop app and added two builder-facing features: a Claude Enterprise Analytics API for tracking team engagement and adoption data, and usage analytics scoped to Cowork sessions. Useful for enterprises benchmarking rollout health.

report.title: Anthropic launches self-hosted sandboxes for Claude Managed Agents in public beta
report.summary: Claude Managed Agents can now run tool execution inside infrastructure you control — your own servers or managed providers including Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, or Vercel — while the agent orchestration loop stays on Anthropic's side. Also adds private MCP server connectivity, giving enterprise teams a cleaner security boundary for agentic workflows.

report.title: Claude Code v2.1.152 ships with per-category usage breakdown and agent-view monitor
report.summary: The latest Claude Code release adds a /usage command that breaks down limit consumption by skills, subagents, plugins, and per-MCP-server costs — giving teams visibility into where token budget goes. The release also adds a unified agent-view screen to monitor all sessions at once and a goal mode that keeps working until a defined condition is met.

report.title: Cohere acquires Aleph Alpha at $20B valuation to build transatlantic sovereign AI challenger
report.summary: Cohere is absorbing Germany's Aleph Alpha — Cohere shareholders retain ~90% of the combined entity — backed by $600M from Schwarz Group (Lidl's parent) as part of a forthcoming Series E. The deal, blessed by Canadian and German governments, targets regulated European enterprises that need data residency and sovereignty guarantees. No new model shipped; deal still pending regulatory close.

report.title: Cohere acquires Reliant AI to launch North for Pharma agentic product
report.summary: Weeks after the Aleph Alpha deal, Cohere acquired Berlin/Montreal biopharma AI startup Reliant AI and is productizing it as 'North for Pharma' — an agentic system for R&D, clinical development, and scientific analytics teams. Existing customers include GSK and Kyowa Kirin; no public API access yet.

learn.name: Antigravity CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's Go-based terminal agent that replaces Gemini CLI with multi-agent support.

detail.whatItDoes:
Antigravity CLI is the terminal surface of Google's Antigravity 2.0 platform, launched at Google I/O 2026 on May 19. It shares the same agent harness as the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app, meaning it can spawn dynamic subagents, call tools, run code in sandboxes, and browse the web from a single prompt in your terminal. The CLI is written in Go for low overhead and keyboard-first remote workflows.

It fully replaces Gemini CLI. Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions stop serving requests for Google AI Pro/Ultra accounts on June 18, 2026. The Antigravity CLI preserves Gemini CLI's key features—Agent Skills, Hooks, Subagents, and Extensions (rebranded as Antigravity plugins)—and adds the multi-agent orchestration layer. It connects by default to Gemini 3.5 Flash at 289 tokens/sec.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend and full-stack engineers who prefer terminal workflows over IDE GUIs, especially those already on Google AI Pro/Ultra or Google Cloud. Teams doing CI/CD pipeline automation, infrastructure provisioning, or multi-step code generation tasks will get the most out of the multi-agent dispatch. Anyone currently using Gemini CLI must migrate before June 18, 2026.
pros: Same agent harness as Antigravity 2.0 desktop—all future improvements apply automatically to CLI too
Spawns dynamic parallel subagents from a single natural-language goal without manual orchestration code
Go-based binary: fast startup, low memory footprint, works well over SSH on remote machines
Free for individuals at launch; integrates with existing Google AI Pro/Ultra subscriptions
cons: Not 1:1 feature parity with Gemini CLI at launch—some extensions may not migrate cleanly
Heavy use requires at least $20/month Google AI Pro; free tier limits are very constrained
Optimized for Gemini models; Claude and GPT-OSS are supported but at higher latency and cost
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS, Linux, or Windows (WSL recommended on Windows)
- A Google account with Google AI Pro/Ultra **or** a Google Cloud project
- No Go installation required—the installer ships a self-contained binary

## 1. Install via the official install script

```bash
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash
```

The installer detects your platform (linux_amd64, darwin_arm64, etc.), downloads the versioned binary, and adds `agy` to your PATH. Verify:

```bash
agy --version
# Antigravity CLI 1.0.0
```

## 2. Authenticate

**Option A — Google Account (personal/Pro/Ultra):**
```bash
agy auth login
# Opens a browser OAuth flow. Accept the permissions.
```

**Option B — Google Cloud project (enterprise/Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform):**
```bash
gcloud auth application-default login
agy config set project YOUR_GCP_PROJECT_ID
agy config set region us-central1
# All agent inference now runs inside your Cloud boundary.
```

## 3. Run your first agent task

```bash
# Single-turn task (headless)
agy "Scaffold a FastAPI app with a /health endpoint and write a pytest suite for it"

# Interactive TUI mode
agy
```

## 4. Define a custom AGENTS.md skill (optional)

Create `AGENTS.md` in your repo root. Antigravity reads it as agent instructions:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md
## Project context
This is a Python monorepo. All new modules go in `src/`. Tests go in `tests/`.
## Preferred tools
- Use `uv` for package management, never `pip` directly.
- Run `pytest -x` before marking any task complete.
```

Then invoke with context:

```bash
agy "Add a Redis cache layer to the user service"
# Agent reads AGENTS.md, follows project conventions automatically.
```

## Gotcha: Gemini CLI migration deadline
If you have `gemini` on your PATH, note that **Gemini CLI stops serving on June 18, 2026** for Pro/Ultra accounts. Your existing scripts that call `gemini` need to be updated to `agy`. The command syntax is largely compatible for simple prompts, but check your extensions—they are now called plugins and need re-registration:

```bash
agy plugins list      # see migrated plugins
agy plugins install PATH_TO_PLUGIN
```

learn.name: ml-intern (Hugging Face)
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source agentic ML engineer that fine-tunes models and ships weights autonomously.

detail.whatItDoes:
ml-intern is an open-source CLI agent from Hugging Face that autonomously handles the post-training research loop: reading papers, searching datasets, writing training code, launching HF Jobs, tracking experiments with Trackio, and uploading trained model weights back to the Hub. It runs an agentic loop of up to 300 iterations with a ContextManager that auto-compacts at 170K tokens and a ToolRouter dispatching to HF docs, repos, datasets, papers, GitHub code search, and external MCP servers. Sensitive operations—paid job launches, destructive commands—pause for explicit user approval.

Every session is auto-uploaded to a private HF dataset in Claude Code JSONL format, making every agent run a debuggable artifact browsable in the HF Agent Trace Viewer. In a benchmark self-improvement run, ml-intern raised a Qwen3-1.7B GPQA score from ~9% to 32% in under 10 hours on a single H100 with no human intervention beyond the initial goal prompt.
detail.whoItsFor: ML researchers and engineers who spend time on fine-tuning, dataset curation, and post-training experiments. Especially useful for academic labs and independent researchers who lack large security teams but want to automate RLHF, dataset distillation, or supervised fine-tuning loops. Works with Anthropic, OpenAI, HF-hosted models, or local models via Ollama/vLLM.
pros: Native Hugging Face ecosystem access: HF Jobs, Hub datasets, Spaces sandbox, Trackio—no custom infra glue needed
Session traces auto-upload to a private HF dataset; every run is reproducible and auditable
Model-agnostic: swap between Claude, GPT-5.5, Llama, or any vLLM/Ollama model with a single flag
Approval gates on expensive/destructive operations prevent runaway spend on cloud compute
cons: Requires HF_TOKEN even for local model runs because it creates private HF Spaces for the sandbox
300-iteration cap and doom-loop detector can interrupt complex multi-stage training pipelines unexpectedly
Autonomous data generation decisions (e.g. synthetic dataset creation) still need human review in sensitive domains
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.11+
- `uv` package manager (`pip install uv` or `brew install uv`)
- A Hugging Face account with a write-access token
- At least one of: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or a local model server

## 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone git@github.com:huggingface/ml-intern.git
cd ml-intern
uv sync
uv tool install -e .
```

Verify the CLI is on your PATH:
```bash
ml-intern --help
```

## 2. Set environment variables

Create a `.env` file or export directly:

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=hf_...             # Required — even for local models (creates private HF Spaces)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... # If using Claude
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...        # If using GPT-5.5
export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...         # For code search tool
# Optional: local model server
export LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000
```

## 3. Run a task

```bash
# Interactive mode (recommended for first run)
ml-intern

# Headless single-prompt mode with a specific model
ml-intern --model anthropic/claude-opus-4-7 \
  "Fine-tune llama3.1-8b on the HuggingFaceH4/ultrafeedback_binarized dataset for 1 epoch, \
   upload weights to my Hub profile as my-llama-sft-run"

# Cap iterations to avoid runaway loops on expensive tasks
ml-intern --max-iterations 50 "your prompt"
```

## 4. Use the HF Sandbox (GPU jobs)

The `--sandbox-tools` flag switches from local execution to an HF Space sandbox with GPU access:

```bash
ml-intern --sandbox-tools \
  "Run a GPQA evaluation on Qwen3-1.7B and report the score"
# Agent will request GPU hardware, create a private HF Space, run the eval, and report results.
```

## 5. Review traces

```bash
# Inside the CLI, toggle trace visibility
/share-traces         # shows current dataset URL
/share-traces public  # makes traces publicly browsable on the Hub
/share-traces private # lock back down
```

## Gotcha: the sandbox always needs HF_TOKEN
Even if you pass `--model ollama/llama3.1:8b` for local inference, the sandbox runtime creates private HF Spaces in the background. The CLI will prompt you on first launch if `HF_TOKEN` is missing, but it will silently disable sandbox features rather than error loudly—so set the token upfront.

learn.name: Gemini Managed Agents API
learn.oneLineDescription: Single Gemini API call provisions a sandboxed Linux agent with persistent state.

detail.whatItDoes:
The Managed Agents API, launched at Google I/O 2026, lets you spin up a fully sandboxed agent with a single call to the Gemini Interactions API. The agent reasons with Gemini 3.5 Flash, calls tools, executes code in an isolated Linux environment, and browses the web. Crucially, each interaction creates an environment that persists across follow-up calls with all files and state intact—enabling multi-turn sessions without reinitializing context.

The agent is powered by the same Antigravity harness that runs Google's own products. You can extend it via markdown skill files (AGENTS.md, SKILL.md) registered as named agents. The API is available now via Google AI Studio and the Interactions API endpoint.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers and product teams that want agentic capabilities embedded inside their own applications or internal tools without managing execution infrastructure. Particularly useful for teams building document processing pipelines, code review workflows, or any multi-step task that currently requires a custom orchestration layer.
pros: One API call replaces an entire orchestration stack: sandboxed Linux env, web browsing, code execution all included
Persistent environment across turns—agent state survives between API calls, no re-upload of files each turn
Customizable via plain markdown AGENTS.md and SKILL.md files; no SDK-specific DSL to learn
Available in Google AI Studio for rapid prototyping before wiring into production
cons: Currently only powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash—no model choice within Managed Agents yet
Execution environment is Google-managed; teams with strict data residency need to route via Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform instead
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- A Google AI Studio account or a Google Cloud project
- A Gemini API key from https://aistudio.google.com/apikey
- Python 3.10+ and `google-genai` SDK

## 1. Install the SDK

```bash
pip install google-genai
```

## 2. Set your API key

```bash
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIza..."
```

## 3. Create and run a Managed Agent

```python
import os
from google import genai
from google.genai.types import GenerateContentConfig

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

# Start an interaction — this provisions the sandboxed agent
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    contents="Clone https://github.com/psf/requests, run the test suite, and return a summary of any failures.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        # Enable the Antigravity agent harness
        tools=[{"managed_agent": {}}],
    ),
)

print(response.text)
```

## 4. Resume a persistent session

The Managed Agents API returns a `session_id`. Pass it on follow-up calls to resume the same sandboxed environment:

```python
# First turn — get session_id from response metadata
session_id = response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].managed_agent_result.session_id

# Follow-up turn — environment (files, state) is intact
response2 = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    contents="Now fix the first failing test and re-run only that test file.",
    config=GenerateContentConfig(
        tools=[{"managed_agent": {"session_id": session_id}}],
    ),
)
```

## 5. Define a custom skill (optional)

Create a file called `SKILL.md` and register it as a named agent in AI Studio, or pass it inline:

```markdown
# SKILL.md
## Project conventions
- All Python must pass `ruff check` before the task is marked complete.
- Use `pytest -x --tb=short` for test runs.
- Never commit secrets; use environment variables.
```

## Gotcha: Managed Agents vs. standard chat
The `managed_agent` tool flag is what triggers sandbox provisioning. Without it, `generate_content` behaves like a normal chat completion. If you forget the flag, your code will appear to work but the agent will not have filesystem or web access.

learn.name: Stainless SDK Generator (pre-acquisition context)
learn.oneLineDescription: OpenAPI-spec-to-SDK generator that powered every official Anthropic SDK—now Anthropic-owned.

detail.whatItDoes:
Stainless converts an OpenAPI specification into production-ready SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, and more—plus CLIs and MCP servers. It was the tool behind every official Anthropic SDK and was also used by OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare, Replicate, and Runway. Anthropic acquired it on May 18, 2026 for a reported ~$300M and is winding down all hosted products (new signups closed). Existing customers keep generated SDKs with full rights to modify and extend them.

Developers who were using Stainless's hosted platform need to migrate. The open-source Stainless CLI still works for local generation from an OpenAPI spec. The acquisition makes SDK and MCP server generation a core part of Anthropic's developer platform, with plans to tighten integration with the Claude API over time.
detail.whoItsFor: API platform teams that need to ship and maintain SDKs in multiple languages without hand-writing each one. Teams that built MCP servers via Stainless are most immediately affected—they need a migration path. Teams evaluating how to connect their APIs to Claude agents should watch for updated Anthropic-native SDK generation tooling in the coming months.
pros: Generated SDKs are idiomatic per language—not mechanical HTTP wrappers—reducing integration friction
MCP server generation from an OpenAPI spec is the fastest path to making your API agent-accessible
Existing generated SDKs and code remain fully owned by customers; no forced migration of the output
cons: Hosted platform is shut down—no new projects, no managed SDK regeneration on API changes
Future development will prioritize Anthropic/Claude integration; OpenAI and Google parity may degrade
No clear ETA on when Anthropic's replacement developer tooling ships with equivalent capabilities
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Using the Stainless CLI locally (post-acquisition fallback)

The hosted product is gone, but the Stainless CLI for local generation still works. This is the recommended path for existing customers who need to regenerate SDKs when their API spec changes.

## Prerequisites
- Node 20+
- Your OpenAPI 3.x spec as a YAML or JSON file
- A Stainless config file (`stainless.yml`) — export it from your old hosted project before the dashboard closes

## 1. Install the Stainless CLI

```bash
npm install -g stainless-api
stainless --version
```

## 2. Generate SDKs locally

```bash
# TypeScript SDK
stainless generate \
  --spec ./openapi.yaml \
  --config ./stainless.yml \
  --language typescript \
  --output ./sdks/typescript

# Python SDK
stainless generate \
  --spec ./openapi.yaml \
  --config ./stainless.yml \
  --language python \
  --output ./sdks/python
```

## 3. Generate an MCP server from your API spec

```bash
stainless generate \
  --spec ./openapi.yaml \
  --config ./stainless.yml \
  --language mcp \
  --output ./mcp-server

cd ./mcp-server && npm install && npm run build

# Test with Claude Code
claude mcp add local ./mcp-server/build/index.js
```

## 4. Wire into CI so SDKs regenerate on spec changes

```yaml
# .github/workflows/sdk-gen.yml
name: Regenerate SDKs
on:
  push:
    paths: ['openapi.yaml']
jobs:
  generate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20' }
      - run: npm install -g stainless-api
      - run: stainless generate --spec openapi.yaml --config stainless.yml --language typescript --output sdks/typescript
      - run: stainless generate --spec openapi.yaml --config stainless.yml --language python --output sdks/python
      - uses: stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v5
        with:
          commit_message: 'chore: regenerate SDKs from updated spec'
```

## Gotcha: export your stainless.yml NOW
The hosted Stainless dashboard is the only place your config lives. If you have not exported it before the platform fully shuts down, local regeneration will produce generic output without your per-language customizations. Log in and export immediately.
